rationale: The batch includes a person name after an introductory phrase and comma; in the representative case, Ben has very low probability because its output root lacks the generic comma-context rule present for other person-name roots. Add the comparable rule for Ben so a name following a comma is supported without hard-coding the observed name choice or asserting that it is the only valid continuation. A comma can occur in other contexts, so this may also increase Ben's probability at some non-introductory commas; the existing alternatives should remain available, and the replay gate must assess that tradeoff.
